answer: A mechanism that actually bites: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because marble only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, echo is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any yarrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
